title: Revisiting Strategic Protectionism in Network Markets
abstract: arXiv:2603.29542v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper studies the welfare effects of an industrial policy targeting a sector with network externalities in a two-country model with strategic trade and R&D investment. When externalities are weak or the goods are close substitutes, the business-stealing effect dissipates more surplus than the externality creates. Under sufficiently strong externalities and weak substitutability or complementarity of the goods, industrial policy competition can make both countries simultaneously better off compared to the laissez-faire outcome because of the mutual business-enhancement effect. The case is stronger for product innovation than for process innovation, as the former directly affects the demand and triggers a stronger network effect than the latter which operates indirectly through the industry supply. translated_title: 重新审视网络市场中的战略性保护主义
translated_abstract: 本文在一个包含战略性贸易与研发投资的双国模型中，研究了针对具有网络外部性产业的产业政策的福利效应。当外部性较弱或商品为近似替代品时，“抢生意效应”所损耗的剩余超过了外部性所创造的剩余。当外部性足够强且商品替代性较弱或为互补品时，由于相互的“生意促进效应”，产业政策竞争可以使两国同时比自由放任情形下的境况更好。这一论点对产品创新比对工艺创新更有说服力，因为前者直接影响需求并引发比后者更强的网络效应，而后者通过行业供给间接发挥作用。因此，网络外部性为双赢的产业政策创造了机会，但其实现取决于市场结构。
tldr: 在具有较强网络外部性且商品替代性较低或互补的市场中，两国间的产业政策竞争可通过相互促进效应实现双赢，而非零和的保护主义博弈。
en_tdlr: In network markets with sufficiently strong externalities and weak substitutability or complementary goods, industrial policy competition between countries can be mutually beneficial through business-enhancement effects, creating opportunities for win-win industrial policies.
